synopsis: ESPE comprises certified non-contact person-detection sensors—light curtains, laser scanners and radar—that trigger protective stops; IEC 61496 and IEC TS 62998 provide their reliability framework [f12388]. Certification covers detection capability, response time and fault behavior, but assumes a stationary machine in a controlled space; IEC TS 61496-5:2023 establishes a radar certification basis while explicitly excluding aspects of moving radar protective-device applications [f12390, f672, f673]. Certified sensors can shorten the component-level safety argument and bound what learned perception must prove, but cannot establish whole-system performance on moving outdoor machines in dust, rain and glare [f12399, f12400, f1039]. IEC TS 62998-1 addresses safety-related sensors outside classic ESPE categories, including mobile and outdoor applications, but Inxpect’s reported use for its radar remains a vendor claim [f12391, f674, f1045]. The safety-rated sensor approach requires certified sensors and a certification body, with Low setup effort through buy-in, Medium relative cost and Low to Medium heavy-off-road maturity [f1041, f1042, f1043, f1044]. Separately, ISO 16001 specifies a 300-millisecond detection time and continuous self-checking for object detection systems, but has no lidar technology annex [f12396, f12397].
